mechanism.originalFailure: The unchanged native lifecycle suite reproduced EBADF on the second reader.next(). The snapshot pinned the adopted recorder descriptor; cloning installed a different primary, but recorder disposal closed the original descriptor without consulting its pins.
mechanism.algorithm: Each store PinLease owns one writer reader hold. Nested holds share that lease. Store close rejects new admissions and drains admitted commits, then writer close retires writes without waiting for consumer-held pins. The physical descriptor remains reachable only through existing positional read capabilities until the last reader hold releases it. That release returns the real physical-close promise. With no reader holds, writer close awaits physical close directly.
mechanism.ownership: This uses the existing descriptor under a counted old-store reader lease. It does not reopen by path or allocate a descriptor per row or pin. State is scalar per writer plus concurrently active leases; no retained history array, reread/replay fallback, or extra journal copy was added.
mechanism.compactionAndShutdown: Pins still exclude compaction. Retirement suppresses deferred compaction and rejects later explicit compaction. Admitted commit planning and effects use serialized unpinned state reads, so closing does not reject admitted checkpoint deletion. Existing clone, native format, commit sequence and group identity rules are unchanged.
mechanism.failures: The final releasing reader receives deferred descriptor-close failure. Reader-free close returns immediate close failure. Raw-stream and callback failures remain first in AggregateError when release also fails, including the original abort reason. Batch/dump owners await their release; mirror flush joins held releases and reports their failure after delivery. Repair and other scoped consumers propagate close promises. A failed physical close does not permanently cache a rejected promise across later owner disposal; no error is swallowed or automatic retry added.
mechanism.closeContract: close/hold release results permit void or Promise<void>, preserving immediate pin invalidation and duplicate-release errors while exposing asynchronous physical-close settlement. No caller is required to finish an iterator before recording shutdown returns.
